This guide continues from the [x402 Quickstart Guide](/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402/quickstart-guide). It adds discovery metadata to a paid endpoint, builds an agent that finds a paid resource through a facilitator's Bazaar and pays it under a spending cap, and lists what changes on mainnet. It uses the stock x402 packages only.

## Before you start

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) and two testnet accounts with a USDC trustline, the buyer's holding some testnet USDC, as set up in the [quickstart](/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402/quickstart-guide#setting-up-a-testnet-wallet). The commands below were run with Node.js 24, `@x402/*` 2.30.0 and `@stellar/stellar-sdk` 16.4.1.

<Warning>

**Install the Stellar SDK version that `@x402/stellar` depends on.** `@x402/stellar` 2.30.0 depends on `@stellar/stellar-sdk` `^16.4.1`. Adding SDK 17 next to it installs two copies of the SDK's XDR classes, which breaks signing at runtime. Check with `npm ls @stellar/stellar-sdk`: it should list a single version.

</Warning>

## Networks, assets and trustlines {#networks-assets-trustlines}

| Network | x402 network id | USDC contract (7 decimals) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Testnet | `stellar:testnet` | `CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA` |
| Mainnet | `stellar:pubnet` | `CCW67TSZV3SSS2HXMBQ5JFGCKJNXKZM7UQUWUZPUTHXSTZLEO7SJMI75` |

A dollar price such as `"$0.01"` becomes USDC on the network you register: `amount: "100000"` of the testnet contract on `stellar:testnet`, of the mainnet contract on `stellar:pubnet`. To charge in another [SEP-41](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0041.md) token, give the price as `{ asset: "<contract id>", amount: "<base units>" }`; the facilitator has to support that asset.

A classic `G…` account needs a trustline to USDC before it can hold it. That applies to the buyer, which sends USDC, and to the seller's `payTo`, which receives it: a payment to a `payTo` without a trustline fails. A contract address (`C…`, for example a smart wallet) needs no trustline.

Every facilitator publishes what it supports at `/supported`. Look for `"scheme": "exact"` on your network with `"extra": {"areFeesSponsored": true}`. A facilitator that catalogs resources for discovery also lists `"bazaar"` in its top-level `extensions`.

## Make an endpoint discoverable {#make-discoverable}

`declareDiscoveryExtension` describes a route's input and output. A facilitator with a Bazaar uses it to catalog the route, and agents use it to call the route without reading your docs.

```bash
mkdir x402-seller && cd x402-seller
npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install express@5 @x402/express@2.30.0 @x402/core@2.30.0 @x402/stellar@2.30.0 @x402/extensions@2.30.0 @stellar/stellar-sdk@16.4.1
```

```js seller.js
import express from "express";
import { HTTPFacilitatorClient, x402ResourceServer } from "@x402/core/server";
import { paymentMiddleware } from "@x402/express";
import {
  bazaarResourceServerExtension,
  declareDiscoveryExtension,
} from "@x402/extensions/bazaar";
import { ExactStellarScheme } from "@x402/stellar/exact/server";

const NETWORK = process.env.NETWORK ?? "stellar:testnet"; // or "stellar:pubnet"
const PAY_TO = process.env.PAY_TO; // the account that receives the payments
const facilitator = new HTTPFacilitatorClient({
  url: process.env.FACILITATOR_URL,
});

const resourceServer = new x402ResourceServer(facilitator)
  .register(NETWORK, new ExactStellarScheme())
  .registerExtension(bazaarResourceServerExtension);

const app = express();
app.use(
  paymentMiddleware(
    {
      "GET /weather": {
        accepts: {
          scheme: "exact",
          price: "$0.01",
          network: NETWORK,
          payTo: PAY_TO,
        },
        description: "Current weather for a city",
        mimeType: "application/json",
        extensions: declareDiscoveryExtension({
          input: { city: "Lisbon" },
          inputSchema: {
            properties: { city: { type: "string", description: "City name" } },
            required: ["city"],
          },
          output: {
            example: { city: "Lisbon", temperature: 21, conditions: "sunny" },
          },
        }),
      },
    },
    resourceServer,
  ),
);
app.get("/weather", (req, res) => {
  res.json({
    city: String(req.query.city ?? "Lisbon"),
    temperature: 21,
    conditions: "sunny",
  });
});
app.listen(4021, () =>
  console.log("listening on http://localhost:4021/weather"),
);
```

```bash
PAY_TO=G... FACILITATOR_URL=https://... node seller.js
```

A seller does not register anywhere. When a payment carrying the `bazaar` extension settles through a facilitator with a Bazaar, the facilitator may add the resource to its catalog. Facilitators validate the metadata and may refuse resources on hosts that are not public, such as `localhost`. The outcome comes back in the `EXTENSION-RESPONSES` header (`success`, `processing`, or `rejected` with a reason), which the stock `HTTPFacilitatorClient` logs. The payment settles whatever the cataloging outcome; deploy the seller on a public host name to be listed.

## Build an agent that discovers and pays {#discover-and-pay}

Facilitators that implement the x402 [Bazaar extension](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/specs/extensions/bazaar.md) can serve their catalog at `GET /discovery/resources` and `GET /discovery/search`:

```bash
curl -s "<DISCOVERY_URL>/discovery/search?query=current%20weather%20for%20a%20city&network=stellar:testnet"
```

`withBazaar` from `@x402/extensions/bazaar` adds the same calls to the stock facilitator client. This agent searches, keeps only results it can pay on testnet for at most 0.05 USDC, fills in the listing's example input, and pays. `spendControls` refuses any payment above the cap before anything is signed.

```bash
mkdir x402-agent && cd x402-agent
npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @x402/fetch@2.30.0 @x402/core@2.30.0 @x402/stellar@2.30.0 @x402/extensions@2.30.0 @stellar/stellar-sdk@16.4.1
```

```js agent.js
import { HTTPFacilitatorClient } from "@x402/core/http";
import { withBazaar } from "@x402/extensions/bazaar";
import {
  decodePaymentResponseHeader,
  wrapFetchWithPaymentFromConfig,
} from "@x402/fetch";
import { createEd25519Signer } from "@x402/stellar";
import { ExactStellarScheme } from "@x402/stellar/exact/client";

const NETWORK = "stellar:testnet";
const MAX_AMOUNT = 500_000n; // 0.05 USDC in base units (7 decimals)

// 1. Discover: search a facilitator's Bazaar for a resource that is paid on this network.
const discovery = withBazaar(
  new HTTPFacilitatorClient({ url: process.env.DISCOVERY_URL }),
);
const { resources } = await discovery.extensions.bazaar.search({
  query: process.argv[2] ?? "current weather for a city",
  network: NETWORK,
  type: "http",
});
const match = resources.find((item) =>
  item.accepts.some(
    (option) =>
      option.network === NETWORK &&
      option.scheme === "exact" &&
      BigInt(option.amount) <= MAX_AMOUNT,
  ),
);
if (match === undefined) throw new Error("no affordable resource found");

// 2. Build the request from the listing's own example input.
const info = match.extensions?.bazaar?.info;
const url = new URL(match.resource);
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(info?.input?.queryParams ?? {}))
  url.searchParams.set(key, value);
console.log(`paying for ${url} (${match.description ?? "no description"})`);

// 3. Pay with the stock client, capped per payment.
const fetchWithPayment = wrapFetchWithPaymentFromConfig(fetch, {
  schemes: [
    {
      network: NETWORK,
      client: new ExactStellarScheme(
        createEd25519Signer(process.env.BUYER_SECRET, NETWORK),
      ),
    },
  ],
  spendControls: { maxAmountPerPayment: "$0.05" },
});
const response = await fetchWithPayment(url);
console.log(response.status, await response.json());
const receipt = response.headers.get("PAYMENT-RESPONSE");
if (receipt !== null) console.log(decodePaymentResponseHeader(receipt));
```

```bash
BUYER_SECRET=S... DISCOVERY_URL=https://... node agent.js "current weather for a city"
```

`DISCOVERY_URL` is any facilitator whose `/supported` lists the `bazaar` extension; the [community facilitators](/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402#community-facilitators) list notes which ones catalog resources. The receipt's `transaction` is the settlement hash; look it up on a block explorer to see the buyer's USDC go to `payTo` and the fee paid by the facilitator. Listings are data supplied by sellers: check the price, network and `payTo` before paying. The agent above checks price and network, and `spendControls` enforces the cap again at signing time.

## What the payer signs {#what-the-payer-signs}

The buyer signs a Soroban authorization entry for exactly one call: `transfer(from = buyer, to = payTo, amount)` on the asset contract named in the requirements. Changing the recipient, the amount or the asset invalidates the signature. The entry expires after about `maxTimeoutSeconds` (the current ledger plus that time divided by the ledger close time), so an unsettled payment cannot be used later. The buyer is not the transaction source, so paying does not use the buyer's sequence number.

## Fee sponsorship {#fee-sponsorship}

`extra.areFeesSponsored: true` means the facilitator pays the network fee of the settlement transaction, so the buyer needs no XLM for that fee. It does not cover account reserves: a classic account still needs its base reserve and the reserve for its USDC trustline (see [Lumens](/docs/learn/fundamentals/lumens#minimum-balance)).

## Moving to mainnet {#moving-to-mainnet}

- **Network.** Use `stellar:pubnet` on both sides. A `"$0.01"` price then resolves to mainnet USDC.
- **Facilitator.** Choose one whose `/supported` lists `exact` on `stellar:pubnet`. Some require an API key, sent from the seller with `HTTPFacilitatorClient`'s `createAuthHeaders` option.
- **RPC.** On mainnet the stock client has no default RPC endpoint and throws without one. Pass one from the [RPC providers](/docs/data/apis/rpc/providers) list: `new ExactStellarScheme(signer, { url: "<mainnet RPC URL>" })`.
- **Accounts.** The buyer and a `G…` `payTo` need trustlines to mainnet USDC (issuer `GA5ZSEJYB37JRC5AVCIA5MOP4RHTM335X2KGX3IHOJAPP5RE34K4KZVN`) and XLM for their reserves.
- **Keys and limits.** Keep secret keys out of code, give agents a separate low-balance account, and set `spendControls` to the most you accept to lose per payment.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `Stellar trustline is missing for account G… and asset C…: HostError: Error(Contract, #13)` when paying | The buyer's `G…` account has no trustline to the asset. Add one (`changeTrust`) and fund it. |
| The facilitator refuses a payment that names a `payTo` without a trustline | `payTo` cannot receive the asset. Add the trustline to the seller's account, or use a `C…` address. |
| `All payment requirements were rejected by spendControls.maxAmountPerPayment` | The price is above the client's cap. Raise the cap only if you mean to pay that much. |
| `Stellar mainnet requires a non-empty rpcUrl` | Pass an RPC URL to `ExactStellarScheme` on `stellar:pubnet`. |
| Signing fails at runtime with XDR type errors | Two versions of `@stellar/stellar-sdk` are installed. Align it with the version `@x402/stellar` depends on. |
| `EXTENSION-RESPONSES` reports `rejected` for `bazaar` | The payment settled, but the facilitator did not catalog the resource. The reason says why. |
